rationale: The buyer is reasonably specific — IT admins and MSPs managing M365 tenants — and the pain (non-obvious multi-step configuration for a task that should be trivial) is a genuine recurring time sink. MSPs in particular bill by the hour, so tools that save configuration time have a clear value proposition and an established software-buying habit. The challenge is that the solution (a guided runbook or configuration wizard) is straightforward to build but is also commoditized: Microsoft's own documentation, community guides, and admin tooling partially cover this ground, making defensibility low and willingness to pay only moderate. Validate whether MSPs will pay before building.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an M365 Mail Routing Configuration Wizard: a step-by-step guided tool that outputs the exact PowerShell commands, connector settings, and transport rule configurations needed for common hybrid/multi-provider email scenarios. The factory builds it as a Claude-powered multi-step form (user answers 5–8 questions about their setup), which generates a tailored configuration guide and copy-pasteable scripts, delivered by email. Stripe handles a one-time fee ($29–$79) or an MSP subscription ($49/month for unlimited runs). Outreach goes to MSP communities (Reddit r/msp, Spiceworks, LinkedIn MSP groups) with operator approval before each batch. Delivery and support are fully automated — Claude handles follow-up questions against a knowledge base. The operator's only recurring task is approving outreach batches. Honest constraint: the content must be kept current as Microsoft updates M365; Claude can handle updates if fed Microsoft's changelog, but the operator needs to flag when major M365 changes ship.
notes: All build_gates are met at this score level, but total (5.6) is below min_total_to_build (6.5), so stage is validate. Defensibility is the main weakness — validate that MSPs will pay before the market gets crowded with free alternatives.
